verdict.summary: Signing people in and posting as them is self-serve once a company Page admin confirms your app. Company pages, ads, sales and recruiting need LinkedIn's partner approval.

whoYouNeed.role: An admin of your company's LinkedIn Page
whoYouNeed.why: Every developer app is tied to a LinkedIn Page, and a Page admin must confirm that link.

whoYouNeed.role: Someone who can describe your business use case
whoYouNeed.why: Partner programs ask what you will build, and the higher tier needs a screen recording.

steps.title: Sign in to the LinkedIn Developer Portal
steps.plain: Log in at linkedin.com/developers with your own LinkedIn account.
steps.whyHuman: Signing in and accepting LinkedIn's API terms are yours to do.

steps.title: Create the app and link your company Page
steps.plain: Create a new app, give it a name and logo, and pick your company's LinkedIn Page.

evidence.note: The Page requirement comes from third-party guides. LinkedIn's own docs we read do not spell it out.

steps.title: Have a Page admin verify the link
steps.plain: In the app's Settings, click Verify next to the Page, generate a link, and send it to a Page admin to approve. The link lasts 30 days.
steps.whyHuman: Only an admin of the company Page can approve.

evidence.note: Third-party sources differ on whether any Page admin or only a super admin can approve.

steps.title: Add the self-serve products
steps.plain: On the Products tab, add 'Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect' and 'Share on LinkedIn'. These need no approval.
steps.technical: Grants openid, profile, email and w_member_social (post, comment and react as the member).

steps.title: Add the redirect address and copy the credentials
steps.plain: On the Auth tab, add the redirect address from your Composio LinkedIn auth config, then paste the client ID and secret into Composio.
steps.whyHuman: The secret is a password for your app. Pasting it yourself keeps it out of any agent's chat history.

steps.title: Apply for Community Management API (only for company pages)
steps.plain: If your agent posts for, or reads analytics from, company pages, apply for the Community Management API. Start with the Development tier, then apply for Standard with a screen recording of each use case.
steps.whyHuman: The application describes your business and use case, and LinkedIn vets you.

steps.title: LinkedIn vets your application (company pages only)
steps.plain: LinkedIn reviews the Development tier request, then the Standard tier upgrade. LinkedIn does not publish how long either takes.

evidence.note: The two tiers and the vetting are sourced. The day range is our estimate. LinkedIn gives none.

steps.title: Apply to the partner program (ads, sales or recruiting)
steps.plain: Each area is its own program: add the Advertising API product from your app's Products tab, or apply to Sales Navigator (SNAP) or the Talent partner programs.
steps.whyHuman: LinkedIn reviews your business and use case.

steps.title: LinkedIn reviews your partner application
steps.plain: LinkedIn does not publish how long partner reviews take.

evidence.note: The programs are sourced; the wait is our estimate.

steps.title: Reading a person's own posts is closed
steps.plain: LinkedIn is not accepting requests for r_member_social. There is no path to this access today; design around it.

forks.condition: Your agent works with ads, Sales Navigator or recruiting
forks.effect: Each is a separate partner program with its own application (Advertising API, SNAP, Talent). Expect a business review, not a form.

forks.condition: Your agent needs to read a member's own posts (r_member_social)
forks.effect: Closed. LinkedIn is not accepting requests for this permission.

nuances.title: Community Management needs a fresh app
nuances.detail: You can only request Community Management Development tier on a new app that has no other API products. If the request button is greyed out, that's why.
nuances.ifStuck: Create a second app tied to the same Page just for the application.

nuances.title: Development tier limits
nuances.detail: Development tier allows 500 requests per app and 100 per member (LinkedIn does not say over what period on this page).
nuances.ifStuck: Plan for Standard tier before a real launch.

nuances.title: API versions expire
nuances.detail: LinkedIn's marketing APIs are versioned monthly and old versions are sunset (for example, November 2025 ends on November 16, 2026).
nuances.ifStuck: Check the version Composio uses if calls start failing after a sunset date.

config.redirectUriNote: Add the redirect URI shown in your Composio auth config on the app's Auth tab.

scopes.name: openid profile email
scopes.plain: Sign the person in and read their name, photo and email.

scopes.name: w_member_social
scopes.plain: Post, comment and react as the person.

scopes.name: w_organization_social
scopes.plain: Post as a company page (needs Community Management approval).

useCases.label: Sign people in, or post as the person who connected
Post for, or read analytics from, company pages
useCases.summary: Community Management API: vetted Development tier, then Standard tier with a screen recording.

useCases.label: Ads, Sales Navigator or recruiting
useCases.summary: Separate partner programs, each with a business review.

evidence.note: Programs are sourced. LinkedIn publishes no timelines; the wait is our estimate.

useCases.label: Read a person's own posts
useCases.summary: Closed: LinkedIn is not accepting requests for r_member_social.

composio.note: You can connect users today with Composio's own LinkedIn app while yours is set up or in review. Users see 'Composio' on the consent screen, rate limits are shared with other Composio customers, and polling triggers run at most every 15 minutes. Switch to your own app when it is ready. LinkedIn Ads is a separate Composio toolkit that needs your own app.

existingApp.summary: Add Composio's redirect address on your app's Auth tab and paste the client ID and secret into Composio. Products you already have approved carry over.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: You want Community Management on an app that already has other products
reReviewTriggers.effect: LinkedIn only accepts Community Management requests from a new app with no other products. Create a second app tied to the same Page.

reReviewTriggers.trigger: You need a new partner product (ads, sales, recruiting)
reReviewTriggers.effect: Each product needs its own application and approval, even on an approved app.
